about.en: A partner who stiffens and sits back from the shoulder throw has their weight on the near heel. Reaping it from the inside as you come out of the turn takes it.

en: Turn in for Seoi-nage with your knees bent and their chest coming onto your back.
Feel them stiffen and sit back, which settles their weight onto the near right heel.
Come out of the turn towards them, keeping both grips and staying low.
Sweep that right heel from the inside with your sole, toes turned in, in the direction their toes point.
Drive both hands down and back towards their right rear corner as the heel goes.
They sit down backwards; keep the sleeve and lift it slightly as they land.

receiving.en: Sitting back against a shoulder throw is sound, and it loads the near heel. When it is swept from the inside there is nothing behind you to step onto, and the arms that were pulling you forward reverse. Ride it backwards rather than trying to stand up out of it: chin tucked, free arm slapping, held arm long. Blocking with your hips instead of settling your weight onto one heel is what keeps the second attack away.

viNotes.en: The defence is read through your back and hands rather than seen: their chest pushing back into you as you turn tells you where their weight has gone. Keep both grips as you come out of the turn, since the reap needs the hands to send them backwards. Sole against heel then does the rest, and it needs no sight.
